caption:
Gemini Notebook, the new name for Google's NotebookLM, can turn your files into an AI podcast.
Upload PDFs, docs, links or YouTube videos, then tap Audio Overview in the Studio panel.
Pick a Deep Dive, a two minute Brief, a Critique or a Debate, in more than 80 languages.
The Standard plan is free with a Gmail account.

What would you turn into a podcast first?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Google · Photo: Google
threads_text: Google's Gemini Notebook, the app formerly called NotebookLM, turns your PDFs, notes and YouTube links into a podcast with two AI hosts, and the basic plan is free. Great for studying, but the hosts can still get facts wrong. What would you feed it first?

slides.headline: Google's free AI turns your boring PDFs into a *podcast*. Here's how

slides.heading: 1. Open a *free notebook*
paras: Go to Gemini Notebook, the new name for Google's NotebookLM, and sign in with your Gmail account.
The Standard plan is free and lets you create up to 100 notebooks.

slides.heading: 2. Drop in *your sources*
paras: Select Add sources and upload PDFs, Word files, slides, audio, web links or public YouTube videos.
Free users can add up to 50 sources per notebook, each up to 500,000 words.

slides.heading: 3. Tap *Audio Overview*
paras: In the Studio panel, select Audio Overview. AI hosts start a discussion about your sources.
It takes a couple of minutes and runs in the background while you keep working.
slides.note: The hosts are AI and can make mistakes.

slides.heading: 4. Pick a *format*
paras: Deep Dive is the default. The Brief gives key takeaways in under two minutes, and Critique and Debate are also there.
You can set the length, pick from 80+ languages and say what to focus on.

slides.hook: Save this for your next exam or long report, and follow for more free AI tricks like this one.
